name: tech.railcore/developers
title: RailCore Developers
description: Indian Railways API docs and code samples, plus your RailCore usage, keys and live test requests.

tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search the RailCore Indian Railways API documentation: guides (authentication, request signing, rate limits, billing in requests), endpoint pages and error codes. Returns the best matching sections with links. Use it for any how-to question about the API.

query.description: What to look for, in plain words or an error code.

kind.description: Limit results to guides, endpoints or errors. Default: any.

tools.name: get_endpoint
tools.description: Details of one RailCore API endpoint: method and URL, parameters, what it costs in requests, the key scope it needs, which plans can use it and whether requests must be signed, response fields and the errors it can answer. Accepts an endpoint id (seat-availability), a method and path (GET /trains/{train_number}/live) or a full URL.

endpoint.description: An endpoint id (seat-availability), a method and path (GET /availability/seats) or a URL.

detail.description: summary (default) or full, which adds response fields and a response example.

tools.name: get_code_sample
tools.description: Working code for a RailCore API endpoint in curl, Node.js, Python, PHP, Go or Java. Set signed to true for Growth, Scale and Enterprise keys, which must sign every request with HMAC-SHA256. Samples read the key from RAILCORE_KEY and the signing secret from RAILCORE_HMAC_SECRET, and work out their dates when they run.

endpoint.description: An endpoint id, a method and path, or a URL.

language.description: curl, node, python, php, go or java.

signed.description: true for Growth, Scale and Enterprise keys, which must sign every request. Default: true only for endpoints that signing plans alone can use.

tools.name: explain_error
tools.description: What a RailCore API error means and how to fix it. Pass the error code (QUOTA_NOT_SUPPORTED), the HTTP status, or the whole error response. Never paste an API key or signing secret; any key-shaped text is removed before it is read.

code.description: The error code, such as QUOTA_NOT_SUPPORTED.

endpoint.description: The endpoint the request went to, if known.

error_json.description: The error response body. Remove any API key or secret first.

tools.name: get_plans
tools.description: RailCore API plans: monthly price in INR, requests a month, per minute and per day, which plans must sign requests, IP allowlists, and which include charts and jobs. Pass a plan name to see one plan.

plan.description: A plan name or id, such as Growth. Leave out to compare all plans.

tools.name: get_my_usage
tools.description: Your RailCore API plan and this month's usage: requests used and left, the per-minute and per-day limits, use per API key and in the docs playground, and when the allowance refills. Requires sign-in to your RailCore account.

tools.name: list_my_keys
tools.description: Your active RailCore API keys: label, the first characters of the key, scopes, whether a signing secret is set, how many IP addresses are allowed, and when each was created, last used and expires. Never a full key or secret. Requires sign-in to your RailCore account.

tools.name: try_endpoint
tools.description: Send one real request to a RailCore API read endpoint with your account and return its answer: status, request ID, requests counted and left, and the response body. It counts against your plan like any API request, so ask the user first. max_requests caps what it may count (default 1); a request that would count more is refused before it is sent. At most 30 tries an hour. Requires sign-in to your RailCore account. The first try also asks permission to make test requests.

endpoint.description: A read endpoint: an id (search-stations), a method and path (GET /stations/search) or a URL.

params.description: Path and query parameters by name, every value as a string, such as {"q": "pune", "limit": "5"} or {"train_number": "12951"}. Dates as YYYY-MM-DD.

body.description: The JSON body as text, for the two POST endpoints only (batch-seat-availability, compare-journeys), such as {"journeys": [{"from": "BSL", "to": "ADI", "date": "2026-12-01"}]}.

max_requests.description: The most requests this try may count, 1 to 25. Default 1. Raise it only after the user agrees to the cost.
